title: Bulgars
fact_summary: The name Bulgar appears in two places on this map: in the Frankish annals, for a people ruled by a khan who became Christian in the 860s, and in archaeology of the Volga region. Whether and how the two are connected is not settled by the sources read so far.

claims.text: The Annals of St-Bertin, under 853, say the Bulgars, allied with the Slavs and lured, so it was said, by Frankish bribes, moved against King Louis of Germany and were defeated.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: Under 864 they say Louis marched to meet the khan of the Bulgars, who had promised to become a Christian. The khan's name is missing in the manuscript; the database supplies Boris.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: Under 866 they report the Bulgar ruler's baptism (“sacrum baptisma suscepit”).
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: A 2022 genetic study describes the Bolshie Tigani and Tankeevka cemeteries in the Volga region as Kushnarenkovo/Karayakupovo culture “mixed with early Bulgars”.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: The Annals of Fulda say that in 895 the “Avars” (Hungarians) invaded the Bulgars' borders and lost a great part of their army, and under 896 that the Greeks ferried them over the Danube into the Bulgar kingdom, where the Bulgars finally won a bloody victory.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in Latin in the scanned edition linked under Sources; the English is Claude's own rendering.

open_questions.text: How were the Bulgars on the Danube related to the Bulgars on the Volga?

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
